intro: Computer-use means giving the model an action space of mouse clicks, keystrokes, and screen reads. It is the most expensive, slowest, most error-prone form of integration. Almost always, an API is the right answer. This page is mostly about NOT using computer-use.

items.title: Vision-grounded (screenshot → action)
items.whenToUse: When the only available interface is a GUI — legacy enterprise apps, hosted dashboards with no API, your own desktop apps.
items.mechanism: Model receives a screenshot, emits a structured action (click at x,y / type text / scroll). Harness executes the action, takes the next screenshot. Loop. Anthropic's Computer Use, OpenAI's Operator, Browser Use.
items.tradeoff: Maximum generality — any GUI. Slow (seconds per step). Brittle to layout changes. High token cost (screenshots are big).

items.title: DOM-grounded (accessibility tree → action)
items.whenToUse: Web automation where you control the harness (Playwright + LLM).
items.mechanism: Instead of pixels, give the model the accessibility tree or a simplified DOM. Actions reference element IDs, not coordinates.
items.tradeoff: Faster, cheaper, more robust than vision-grounded. Limited to web. Still slower than an API.

items.title: Agentic browser products
items.whenToUse: End-user task automation on the open web (book a flight, fill a form).
items.mechanism: Vendor-managed browser + agent. You give a goal, they execute. Examples: Computer Use API, Browser Use, browserbase, Manus.
items.tradeoff: Removes the harness burden; adds vendor lock-in + per-task pricing. Pre-built sandbox + retry logic.

items.title: Task recipes (deterministic with LLM repair)
items.whenToUse: Repetitive workflows where the happy path is well-known but edge cases break naive scripts.
items.mechanism: Record a Playwright/Selenium script for the happy path. Wrap each step in a try-catch; on failure, call the LLM with the current screenshot + script context, ask for a one-shot repair action.
items.tradeoff: Cheap and fast in the common case. LLM is only paid for when the brittleness shows up. Maintenance cost lives in the recipes, not the model.

items.title: When NOT to use computer-use
items.mechanism: Check for: (a) an HTTP/gRPC API, (b) a CSV/JSON export, (c) a database connection, (d) a webhook. If any exists, use it. Computer-use is the option of last resort, not first.
items.tradeoff: An API call is 50–500× faster and cheaper, with deterministic behavior and structured outputs. There is no contest when an API exists.

pitfalls.title: Scaling trap
pitfalls.body: Computer-use that works at 10/day costs $50. The same workflow at 10,000/day costs $50,000 and now needs a fleet of browsers. The cost shape does not look like an API.

pitfalls.title: Screenshot token overhead
pitfalls.body: A full-page screenshot is 1500–3000 vision tokens. Multiply by 20 steps × 1000 tasks/day — vision tokens dominate the bill. Crop and compress.

pitfalls.title: CAPTCHAs and bot detection
pitfalls.body: Targets that detect automation will increasingly block agentic browsers. Plan for it; build manual-fallback paths into your workflows.

pitfalls.title: No undo
pitfalls.body: An agent that clicks the wrong button submits a form. There is no transactional rollback over a GUI. Wrap destructive workflows in human approval gates.

pitfalls.title: Credential handling
pitfalls.body: Passing credentials into a screenshot-driven agent means they may show up in screenshots, traces, logs. Use injected credential handlers, scrub from traces, never let the model see secrets directly.

artifact.content:
<!-- Decision prompt: should I use computer-use here? -->

Before touching computer-use, answer these IN ORDER. Stop at the first YES.

1. Is there a public HTTP/gRPC API for this task? → USE THE API.
2. Is there a SOAP / legacy-RPC interface? → USE IT (yes, even SOAP).
3. Is there a webhook or scheduled export I can consume? → USE IT.
4. Is there a CLI or admin tool? → SHELL OUT.
5. Is there a database I can read or write directly? → USE THE DB.
6. Is there an RPA platform already in place? → PIPE THROUGH IT.
7. Do I have ownership of the target UI? → ADD AN API ENDPOINT INSTEAD.

If you got here with no YES, computer-use is plausible. Now ask:
- Volume: do I really need >100/day, or is this a one-off? (One-offs: just do it yourself.)
- Cost: am I comfortable with $1–5 per task and 30–120s wall-clock?
- Reliability: can I tolerate 5–15% failure rate before recovery?

If all three are 'yes' — proceed with computer-use, and budget a retry + human-fallback path from day one.
